easy.q: What does Elder Gilbert believe will be the hallmark, or special sign, of Christ’s disciples in the last days?
options: Winning debates about religion
Teaching truth with love
Keeping away from people who disagree
easy.why: Elder Gilbert said, “I believe teaching truth with love will be the hallmark of Christ’s disciples in the last days.” Truth and love belong together.

easy.q: A stake president took Elder Gilbert to a home where five people were waiting, each with a different concern. What did Elder Gilbert do for nearly two hours?
options: He listened to their stories
He taught them a long lesson
He read scriptures aloud to them
easy.why: The Spirit kept prompting him to wait, so he listened. Afterward he invited them to stake conference, and each one accepted.

easy.q: According to Elder Gilbert, what is the best way to help someone else keep their covenants?
options: Remind them often of their mistakes
Wait until they ask you for help
Keep your own covenants
easy.why: This is part of being a light. Elder Gilbert taught, “The best way to help someone else keep their covenants is to keep your covenants.”

easy.q: Elder Gilbert once answered a struggling friend with angry words. He said he may have won the debate, but what did he lose?
options: His written notes
The Spirit
His turn to speak
easy.why: He said, “I lost the Spirit and I failed to help my struggling friend.” That day he stood for truth, but without love.

easy.q: Elder Gilbert repeated an invitation President Nelson once gave. What did he invite all of us to do?
options: List the people who most need this talk
Stop talking with people who disagree
Look deeply into our own hearts
easy.why: Elder Gilbert worried some would see only others’ shortcomings. Like President Nelson, he invited each of us to look into our own heart first.

medium.q: Why did Elder Gilbert mention Sister Dennis’s story of the wounded dog that would not respond to her owner?
options: To show that hurt people usually cannot be reached
To show that what looks like hostility may be hidden pain
To show that we should keep away from angry people
To show that kindness matters more than truth
medium.why: He taught, “Sometimes what we perceive as hostility may actually be someone’s hidden pain or regret.” Tense moments can hide what is really wrong.

medium.q: In the home visit, Elder Gilbert was tempted to interject but waited. What did he say resisting that impulse accomplished?
options: It showed the family that he agreed with them
It kept the visit short enough for his schedule
It let the stake president do the teaching
It built common ground so he could later teach with love
medium.why: He said resisting the impulse to respond “built common ground, which allowed me later to teach from a place of love.” Listening came before teaching.

medium.q: After the tense meeting with academic leaders, a university chancellor later sought Elder Gilbert’s counsel. What lesson did he draw from this?
options: Being a light opens more doors than pointed arguments
Silence is always the right answer to criticism
Strong arguments earn respect in the end
Academic leaders rarely change their minds
medium.why: Elder Gilbert said, “Being a light opens more doors than any pointed argument ever will.” The chancellor asked for help creating a course on character.

medium.q: Elder Gilbert quoted President Christofferson about the two great commandments. What does putting the first commandment first do to our ability to love our neighbor?
options: It limits it to those who share our faith
It sets it aside until we are more faithful
It amplifies and strengthens it
It leaves it much the same as before
medium.why: President Christofferson taught that loving God first “elevates our ability to love others more fully and perfectly” because we partner with God in caring for His children.

medium.q: Elder Gilbert quoted President Nelson contrasting two kinds of messages. How does Heavenly Father communicate?
options: Loudly and boldly, so no one can ignore it
Simply, quietly, and with stunning plainness
Mostly through dramatic signs and wonders
In ways that only the learned can grasp
medium.why: President Nelson said the adversary’s messages are “loud, bold, and boastful,” while Heavenly Father speaks simply and quietly. Elder Gilbert added that Christ modeled this perfectly.

hard.q: Elder Gilbert quoted President Holland on a “crucial difference” the Savior understood. Which response to a friend who has wronged you best fits it?
options: Forgiving him only after he admits that he was wrong
Deciding the wrong was not really wrong, to keep the peace
Forgiving him freely without calling the wrong right
Withholding forgiveness so he learns it was serious
hard.why: President Holland said there is “a crucial difference between the commandment to forgive sin” and “the warning against condoning it.” The Savior forgave freely yet never condoned sin.

hard.q: According to Elder Gilbert, what happens when we try to love others by minimizing God’s laws?
options: We separate ourselves from the One who loves them most
We earn their trust and can teach them later
We lose their respect for what we believe
We make the commandments seem harder to them
hard.why: He taught that in doing so “we separate ourselves from the one person who loves them the very most.” The Savior both loved and said, “go, and sin no more.”

hard.q: A woman’s beliefs are attacked in a heated group discussion. Which response best fits how Elder Gilbert applied “avoid overly contentious settings” with the academic leaders?
options: She lets it rest, having decided her critics are probably right
She lets it rest for now, still disagreeing, and stays open to talk later
She makes one last sharp point for the record and then lets it rest
She lets it rest and resolves never to discuss faith with them again
hard.why: He “chose at least for that setting to table the discussion despite my strong disagreement.” His quiet was neither agreement nor a closed door; later a university chancellor reached out to him for counsel.

hard.q: Elder Gilbert said teaching truth with love will ask different things of different people. Which two did he name?
options: Greater knowledge for some, greater patience for others
Greater conviction for some, greater charity for others
Greater courage for some, greater caution for others
Greater faith for some, greater obedience for others
hard.why: He said, “For some this will require greater conviction. For others it will demand greater charity.” Each of us may lean too far toward only truth or only love.

hard.q: Which everyday situation is most like the mistake Elder Gilbert said he made with his friend who was attacking the Church?
options: Agreeing with a friend’s criticisms just to keep the peace
Staying quiet while a coworker criticizes your beliefs
Sending a sharp, accurate reply to a relative’s criticism
Listening a long while before sharing your testimony
hard.why: Elder Gilbert “shot back an angry retort.” He said, “That day I stood for truth, but I did it without love and without charity.” Being right was not enough.
